# Talk about making love before you do it

I use “making love” differently from just having sex. Making love, to me, is when two people who care about each other deeply and feel super connected use sex as part of that connection. If you’ve never experienced that kind of love, explaining it may be like explaining the taste of an orange. If you don’t know what love is, you don’t know; I’d suggest starting with my inner-child reparenting guide instead.

Having sex is the physical act itself, whether that connection is there or not, and sometimes the act creates more of the connection too.

The awkward part is that most couples wait until they’re already having sex to talk honestly about it. That is about the worst time to discover that saying what you want disappoints the naked person in front of you.

Before then, I want to know what actually makes her body relax and open, what simply doesn’t work for her, and whether there’s anything kinky she needs to be able to say out loud. I want her to know the same things about me. Our pasts may have made either of us want certain things or avoid them, and neither of us has to know all the answers yet. “I don’t know, but I’m willing to find out honestly with you” is a perfectly good answer.

I also want to know what sex is for her. Maybe she mainly thinks of bonding and I mainly think of play, or vice versa. Sometimes it may feel sacred; another time it may just be how we come down from a bad day. It doesn’t have to mean the same thing every time.

And sex drive won’t stay put. For some stretch one of us is going to want more, less, or something different. That mismatch can turn into a really sad quiet resentment. We can’t solve a future mismatch in advance, but I’d rather know how we plan to talk about it before either person is already hurt.

The question I care about most is whether we can still say what’s true once we’re naked. If I think she’ll be disappointed, can I tell her anyway? Can she do the same with me? Talking before our clothes come off is already part of making love to me, because bodies fitting well doesn’t tell me whether we can stay honest while we’re completely exposed.

## Can Casual Sex or a Situationship Actually Be Honest?

Your body doesn’t know that you picked someone up at a bar and agreed it was only for fun. Oxytocin, vasopressin, and the rest can start attaching you anyway. Then the next morning, you’re wondering why they didn’t call. Well, not getting pulled in any further is the best outcome still available, actually, since you just played Russian Roulette with a potential life bond to a stranger.

“I don’t know whether I want something serious with you. I’m not pretending I do. I’d still like to have sex.”

That may be candid about what you expect now. It doesn’t settle what either of you will owe if the act creates something neither of you expected. Sex can make a child. If this girl gets pregnant, she’s gonna call you. Then what? You block her? Agree to child support? Try to convince her to abort when she thinks abortion is killing her child? This is what penetrative sex can do. No contraception is perfect.
